To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lipoplexes based on DOTAP:Cholesterol (1:1) were the most efficient in transfection of primary cortical neurons and C6 glioma cell lines, that the use of transferrins associated with lipoplexes resulted on higher levels of gene expression in C6 and primary cortical neurons and that the levels and duration gene expression in primary cortical neurons are higher than in primary hippocampal cells.
the cationic lipid DOTAP/Cholesterol (1:1) was the best liposome formulation to transfer DNA into glioma cells, hippocampal, and cortical neurons.
lipoplexes based on DOTAP:Cholesterol (1:1) are the best formulation to transfect C6 glioma, hippocampal, and cortical neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methodologies to transfer genes into neurons, which can be applied to gene therapy of neurological diseases.
the development of new strategies and methods for the efficient and safe transfer of genes into the CNS, which may be useful for gene therapy of neurodegenerative diseases.
the improvement of lipoplexes for gene delivery into neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best formulation of lipoplex to transfer a reporter into C6 gliomas and primary hippocampi neurons is DOTAP:DOPE:Chol (5:4:1 mol ratio), whereas for primary cortical neurons it is DOTAP:Cholesterol (1:1).

the use of transferrins associated to cationic liposomes is a promising tool for gene delivery into neurons, particularly into cortical neurons, and that the levels of transduction can be further improved by the use of the best cationic lipid formulation, i.e., DOTAP:Cholesterol (1:1).
the use of transferrins-associated lipoplexes can improve transfection activity and duration of gene transfection in C6 glioma and primary neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of transferrins as a targeting ligand associated to DOTAP:Cholesterol-based lipoplexes is a promising approach to improve gene transfer into the CNS.

the use of Tf-associated lipoplex formulation can be used for gene transfer into neurons, and that the use of cortical neurons as a model to investigate gene transfer into the CNS is more promising than the use of hippocampal neurons.
the transferrin-associated DOTAP/Chol (1/1 mol ratio) lipoplexes are the most efficient carriers of DNA into C6 cells, primary hippocampus and cortical neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of a gene delivery system for the treatment of neurological disorders requires a thorough knowledge of the cell type and the stage of development of the cells to be transfected.
the use of Tf-associated DOTAP/Chol lipoplexes can be a promising approach for gene therapy of CNS disorders.
it is possible to achieve a significant gene transfer into primary neurons, and that the use of Tf-associated lipoplex can be a valuable tool to improve gene transfer into the brain.
